decisions.decision: Split the outcome into three stages and scope V2-064 to the first: register a Repository through the API and reach real GitHub read-only. Stage 2 and stage 3 need NEW task ids, which the coordinator must assign: V2-065 through V2-070 already exist as unrelated task-states (human-input surface, release surface, provider registry, scheduler wiring, runner version, record envelope), so the successors are proposed as V2-071 and V2-072 and their ids are the coordinator's to confirm. Stage 2 (proposed V2-071) outcome: 'Give each Increment a real Git working copy inside the confined Runner workspace -- cloned from a real Git remote, branched, changed, verified and committed, with the working copy's path, symlink, git-common-dir and ownership validated and no write outside the workspace -- so a change exists as an Artifact Observation rather than only as an Execution record.' It also carries the Requirement-to-Repository association (d13) and the ServiceConfig.RepositoryID repair (d14). Stage 3 (proposed V2-072) outcome: 'Reach the registered forge with a verified Increment: push its branch to the registered GitHub repository under the external-effect protocol -- operation_id, expected version, fencing token, outbox, read-after-write observation, needs-input when undecidable -- against an owner-designated sandbox repository with a bounded and reversible blast radius, so a Requirement produces a reviewable change on the real forge.' V2-064's outcome sentence is delivered by the trio, not by V2-064 alone, and V2-064 claims only cap-repository-registration.
decisions.rationale: The union of the three clauses touches nine CI components (domain, application, store-memory, store-firestore, api, web, contracts, runner, docs), adds a new domain aggregate, a new public API contract path, two persistence adapters, an owner UI surface, a Source Control Adapter, an Integration Adapter and a live forge write. Its verification character also changes three times: deterministic local closure, real-kernel git integration (docs/architecture/validation.md L84 forbids faking git, namespace and signals), and live forge evidence with recorded identifiers (docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md L126-130, G3.1). Worse, the write leg has no sanctioned target: docs/architecture/validation.md L124 requires a dedicated sandbox Repository for anything not confirmable read-only, and no such repository is designated. One Work Order cannot carry three verification regimes and an unresolved external prerequisite. Registration is also the strict prerequisite of the other two: nothing can be cloned that was never registered, so stage 1 is not throwaway work.

decisions.decision: Repository identity is a loop-issued opaque repository_id. The forge coordinates are a separate value object, the source locator: forge (constant "github"), host, owner, name, default_branch. Uniqueness is enforced on the normalised (forge, owner, name) triple per Installation; the clone URL is never the identity and is derived from the locator, never stored as the key.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/domain-model.md L36-37 already separates '`repository_id`' from 'source locator and default branch', so this is the declared model rather than an invention. Every other identifier in internal/domain is an opaque string produced through opaqueID and s.ids.Next (internal/domain/model.go L13-48), so an opaque repository_id is the established form. A URL is the wrong key on measurement as well as on principle: a GitHub rename or transfer changes owner/name while the repository is the same object, and some URL forms can carry a credential, which docs/policies/README.md L39 forbids from ever entering a canonical record. Normalising and comparing the triple is what actually prevents the same repository being registered twice, which a raw-URL key would not (git@ vs https, trailing .git, case).

decisions.decision: The Repository aggregate is a new file internal/domain/repository.go carrying its own ValidateRepository and DecideRepository. internal/domain/model.go's generic Validate and Decide switches are not extended, and internal/domain/model.go, control.go, lease.go, release.go and id.go are prohibited paths.
decisions.rationale: Measured precedent: internal/domain/control.go, lease.go and release.go each declare an aggregate and its functions entirely outside model.go's generic pair. Validate's type switch handles only *Requirement/*Increment/*Execution/*Lease and their value forms; Decide handles only Requirement and Increment. ControlIntent, the largest domain surface in the package, appears in neither. Following that precedent keeps V2-064's domain change to one additive new file and makes the M1 proven-closed surface in model.go a prohibited path rather than a place the implementer has to be trusted not to disturb. It is the strongest available scope control on the riskiest file in the repository.

decisions.decision: Registration is an owner operation over the existing Authenticator/RoleOwner seam with no new authentication mechanism: LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator (V2-051) preview-local, CombinedAuthenticator/IAP in production, exactly as /v1/requirements is gated today. A Repository belongs to the Installation, never to a person and never to a Runner. The record carries RequestedBy for attribution only and no assignee, no ACL and no per-person view.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/domain-model.md L19-20 makes the Installation the owner of Repository, Runner, Provider Account and policy; a Repository is therefore not a person's property. That matches the operating shape exactly: Repository-to-person is 1:n and person-to-machine is 1:n precisely because the Repository is shared through the Installation while machines are not shared at all, so the record must carry no machine identity and no person identity as an authorization subject. internal/domain/model.go L218-231 already establishes RequestedBy as an identity reference that the domain never interprets, authenticates or authorizes -- the correct and only slot for who registered it. Multi-person task management is out of scope, so anything resembling an assignee field would be speculative surface that the declaration does not ask for.

decisions.decision: Four routes, following the repository's own literal-path and {id}:verb conventions in internal/api/api.go and contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml: POST /v1/repositories (register, owner), GET /v1/repositories (list, owner), GET /v1/repositories/{repository_id} (detail, owner), POST /v1/repositories/{repository_id}:observe (runner) and POST /v1/repositories/{repository_id}:retire (owner). Retire is a domain transition registered -> retired; a Repository is never deleted.
decisions.rationale: The declaration's rollback condition is '登録前のInstallation状態へ戻し、他Repositoryへ影響が残っていないことを確認する' and promotion prerequisite 条件4 requires rollback to be confirmed, so a registration with no reversal cannot satisfy the contract it is built against; omitting retire would weaken the declaration by making one of its three outcome_conditions unobservable. Deletion is the wrong reversal because docs/architecture/domain-model.md L384 retains referenced entities until the rollback window closes, and every other aggregate in this codebase reverses by transition (IncrementAbandoned, RequirementStatus) rather than by removal. The verb-suffix form is not invented here: /v1/leases/{lease_id}:renew and /v1/executions/{execution_id}:start already exist in both the router and the OpenAPI document.

decisions.decision: The Control Plane never invokes gh or git. Registration records the source locator with reachability unobserved. The read-only GitHub probe runs on the Runner and is submitted back as a bounded Repository Observation (reachable, default_branch, can_push, forge identity, adapter version, observed_at). The detail view derives 'ループが実行可能かとその理由' from that Observation, and reports 'not yet observed' when none exists.
decisions.rationale: Three independent constraints force the probe onto the Runner. docs/architecture/decisions/index.md D26 and docs/policies/README.md L42 keep credentials Runner-local and Runner access repository-, operation-, revision- and fencing-token-scoped; docs/architecture/overview.md states the Control Plane holds no Provider CLI credential, and the production Control Plane is Cloud Run with no gh binary and no gh credential store, so a synchronous probe there is not merely wrong but impossible. docs/architecture/domain-model.md L7-8 and docs/policies/README.md L16 independently require that Git and VCS state enter as an Observation and never as canonical state. The precedent is already in the ports: domain.RunnerObservation with RunnerObservationRepository (internal/application/ports.go L194-197) is the same shape. This also stops the design from fabricating the executability field: it is measured or it is explicitly unobserved, never invented.

decisions.decision: The forge client is the gh CLI as a subprocess in internal/runner/forge.go. Not an HTTP client, not go-github. granted_names stays the empty array and the credential is never touched by our code.
decisions.rationale: Measured: gh is present at /usr/bin/gh, version 2.92.0 (2026-04-28), authenticated to github.com as wakuwaku3 with scopes gist/project/read:org/repo/workflow, and api.github.com answers (gh api rate_limit returned limit 5000, remaining 5000). go-github is not merely undesirable but unavailable: go.mod and go.sum are prohibited paths, so no dependency can be added at all. V2-017 d8's doctrine transfers verbatim -- gh reads its own store at ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml (measured present) and takes no credential from argv or environment, so credential isolation is proven as an absence and the Secret Broker has nothing to hand over, satisfying docs/policies/README.md L39-42 without a grant. An HTTP client would require the token to enter this process's environment, which is the one thing the whole credential design exists to prevent. internal/runner is also the only component root where this file can live without creating a new CI component.

decisions.decision: Resolve the gh executable to an absolute path and assert filepath.Base(path) == "gh" before exec, using the existing internal/runner/confinement.go resolveTool pattern (PATH first, then /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin, /sbin). Record the resolved absolute path and the gh version in evidence.
decisions.rationale: Measured directly: inside devbox run --pure, git IS on PATH (.devbox/nix/profile/default/bin/git, devbox-provided) but gh is NOT on PATH at all, while /usr/bin/gh exists. A bare exec.Command("gh", ...) therefore works on the host and fails in the validated environment -- the exact failure V2-017 d6 hit with the claude CLI and solved this way. resolveTool already exists in this package for precisely this reason, so this is reuse rather than new mechanism, and the basename assertion is what keeps an attacker-controlled path from substituting another binary.

decisions.decision: Record now, for stage 3 to consume: no git credential.helper is configured at repository or global scope on this machine, so a bare git push over HTTPS cannot authenticate. The push leg must use a per-invocation git -c credential.helper='!<absolute gh> auth git-credential'. It must not run gh auth setup-git and must not mutate global git config, and the token must never appear in argv or the environment.
decisions.rationale: Measured: git config --get-all credential.helper is empty at both local and global scope; origin is an https remote (https://github.com/wakuwaku3/agentic-loop-foundation.git); gh auth git-credential exists in gh 2.92.0 ('Implements git credential helper protocol'). This is a latent trap that would surface only at the first push, in the stage that has the least slack, so it is measured and written down here rather than rediscovered there. Per-invocation -c is chosen over setup-git because docs/policies/README.md L14-15 refuses console-only or ambient machine configuration as a source of truth, and mutating the owner's global git config is a side effect outside any declared workspace.

decisions.decision: V2-064 reaches real GitHub read-only and only read-only: gh api repos/{owner}/{name} for existence, default_branch and viewer push permission. No branch, no ref, no PR, no repository creation. Because that reach succeeds today with the owner's existing gh authentication, V2-064 requires no human intervention and must not be recorded as external-unavailable.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md L126-130 (G3.1) accepts a GitHub condition only on live evidence carrying the resource's identifiers and refuses local, emulator or fake substitutes, and L359 requires unavailability to be measured rather than assumed. The reach was measured available (d7), so the honest state is available. The blast radius of a read is nil, which is what makes it safe to make it a gate-bearing live check. Conversely docs/architecture/validation.md L124 requires a dedicated sandbox Repository for anything not confirmable read-only, and no such repository is designated, so a write leg in V2-064 would either violate that rule or need an approval this task cannot obtain. Read-only is therefore both the maximum honest reach and the correct one.

decisions.decision: Stage 3's external-unavailable form, written here so its blocker is not improvised: status blocked, block_reason "external-unavailable: an owner-designated GitHub sandbox repository for reversible branch-push and PR exercises; needs: the owner to designate or create one and name its owner/name in the task state", next_owner sol. Substituting a local bare repository for that live leg is prohibited.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md L266-282 fixes exactly this shape (blocked, block_reason 'external-unavailable: <resource>; needs: <input>', next_owner sol) and L277-278 prohibits registering fake, emulator or local results as live-equivalent. docs/architecture/validation.md L124-126 requires the reversible exercise to happen in a dedicated sandbox Repository within an explicit test resource and hard budget. There is a second, sharper reason not to improvise a target: docs/architecture/validation.md L187 records that gitleaks git scans every ref in the repository, not just HEAD, so any probe branch left behind keeps the gate red -- pushing probe commits into the Foundation's own repository would couple the live exercise to the secret gate.

decisions.decision: cap-autonomous-resolution's minimum, derived mechanically from its declaration rather than negotiated. Its success condition names 分解, 変更, 検証, Preview観測 and its stages add 統合 and Stable反映. 分解 exists (Service.Plan). 変更 and 検証 both require a real working copy: a code change and a verification run inside it -- absent today, and stage 2's whole content. 統合 requires an Integration Adapter emitting commit/branch/push -- absent today, stage 3's. A PR is explicitly NOT required. Preview観測 is unreachable while V2-014 is external-unavailable, so this capability cannot be closed by V2-064 and its two successors together, and none of them may claim it.
decisions.rationale: The 'PR is optional' reading is not a convenience, it is stated four times independently: docs/policies/README.md L67 'PRs are optional integration adapters. Human review is not a completion gate', docs/architecture/overview.md L197 'PRは任意であり、人間reviewを待たない', docs/principles.md L22 'RequirementとPRを1対1に固定しない', docs/product/definition.md L297 '最終成果物はPRではなく、ループによって改善されるApplicationである'. So the minimum reviewable artefact is a pushed branch recorded as an Artifact Observation, not a PR. The Preview limitation must be stated rather than papered over: the declaration's observable_result requires Preview観測結果 and Stable反映状況 on the Requirement detail, and inventing either would be exactly the fabrication the gate rules forbid. Naming the gap is how the declaration stays un-weakened while the task stays honest.

decisions.decision: The Requirement-to-Repository association is deferred to stage 2 (proposed V2-071). V2-064 adds no field to domain.Requirement.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/domain-model.md L52 does model '関連Repository集合' on Requirement, and internal/scheduler already carries Requirement.RepositoryIDs, so the association is real -- but its only consumer is the working copy that decides what to clone, which is stage 2's content. Adding an unread field would mean touching internal/domain/model.go, the M1 proven-closed struct, for no observable outcome in this task, and would forfeit d3's scope control. The RequestedBy precedent shows the additive pattern is available when it is actually needed.

decisions.decision: Do not repair application.ServiceConfig.RepositoryID in V2-064. Record the measurement as debt owned by stage 2 (proposed V2-071): it is never set in production, so ControlTarget.RepositoryID is always the empty string on every existing call site, and a ScopeRepository Control Intent can therefore never match anything.
decisions.rationale: Measured: ServiceConfig has a RepositoryID field (internal/application/service.go L135) consumed at L434, L734 and L1088 to build ControlTarget, but cmd/control-plane/main.go L172 constructs ServiceConfig with InstallationID and LeaseTTL only, leaving RepositoryID empty. domain.matches (internal/domain/control.go L138) compares target.RepositoryID against the scope value, so ScopeRepository (declared at control.go L26 and accepted by the API at service.go L82) is dead in production. Fixing it means changing target construction on the Heartbeat, Prepare and AcceptResult paths, which are fence-bound and covered by the M1 closure tests; that belongs with the Increment-to-Repository link that gives those paths a repository to name, not with registration. Registration is what finally makes a repository id exist to be named, so recording the debt here is the point at which it becomes actionable.

decisions.decision: Bound the observation write: every Service mutation reserves Firestore quota through s.mutate, so the Runner submits an observation only when none exists, when the stored one is older than a bounded staleness interval evaluated against an injected clock, or when the locator changed. It is idempotent by request_id like every other mutation. No wall-clock timer, no goroutine.
decisions.rationale: internal/application/service.go L126 reserves quota.MutationUsage per mutation key, and internal/application/ports.go L206-212 requires the reservation to fail closed at 80% of the daily budget, so an observation submitted on every heartbeat would spend the Installation's write budget on telemetry. docs/architecture/validation.md L211-215 and the repository's standing determinism rule make an injected clock with bounded polling the only admissible form of 'periodically'.

decisions.decision: Two verification regimes, strictly separated. Local closure inside make check: the aggregate's decide/validate closure, locator normalisation and the duplicate-locator conflict, registration and retire idempotency and control gating, both stores, the four routes' role/JSON/origin/error contract, the OpenAPI path presence, the owner UI render, and the gh adapter's argv construction and every refusal path -- all without invoking gh. Live-gated outside make check, behind AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_FORGE=1: the single read-only gh api probe against the real repository.
decisions.rationale: The split follows docs/architecture/validation.md L17-18, which refuses to let either automated tests or live exercise substitute for the other. Gating by environment variable and skipping otherwise is the measured house pattern (internal/api/live_local_test.go L179-185, internal/runner/provider_live_test.go L37-38), and devbox run --pure strips the environment so the gate cannot fire by accident and -e is required to set it. The negative assertions about the adapter (wrong basename refused, missing executable refused, non-empty granted_names refused) must be deterministic and therefore must not need the network, while the reachability claim must be live and therefore must not be deterministic. Neither can be tested in the other's regime.

decisions.decision: Nine evidence records, one per component whose roots this task touches: domain, application, store-memory, store-firestore, api, web, contracts, runner, docs. No task-ledger record is issued; the residual staleness is recorded as a note, as V2-059 did.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md L252-253 makes the evidence key a per-component value read from the final green tree, so one record per component is the only grouping in which each key means what it says. task-ledger's root is .agents/** and the evidence artefacts themselves live there, so a task-ledger key is self-referential; docs/architecture/validation.md L267-273 defines a two-commit attestation protocol for that case, which V2-059 did not invoke and which would double this task's ceremony for no new proof. Note also that control-plane's key moves without its roots changing, because contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is one of its declared contract_dependencies -- recorded, not repaired, since ci/components.json is V2-045's.

decisions.decision: Do not edit contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json, and do not add /v1/repositories to cap-repository-registration's owner_surfaces. Record the observation for the coordinator instead.
decisions.rationale: The declaration must not be rewritten to match the result, and the capability's promotion prerequisite 条件8 is satisfied by adding the path to contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, which this task does. The existing owner_surfaces value /owner/ already resolves under internal/contracts TestReleaseContract's check (release_contract_test.go L236-243 accepts /owner/ or any declared OpenAPI path), so nothing is broken by leaving it. Adding a surface would be a strengthening rather than a weakening, but it is still a change to the release contract, and the release contract is the coordinator's to move.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_FORGE=1 -- go test -count=1 -v -run TestForgeReachabilityLive ./internal/runner
risks: Nine components in one Work Order is the largest surface any v2 task has carried. The mitigation is a fixed implementation order (domain, application ports and service, memory store, api and openapi, firestore, web, runner forge adapter, live probe, evidence) with a mid-task escalation trigger: if the domain and application legs are not green before the api leg begins, stop and escalate rather than carrying a broken seam forward.

make ownership fails on any tracked file not assigned to a component, and ci/components.json is prohibited. Every new file must land under an existing component root -- which is exactly why the forge adapter goes to internal/runner and not to a new internal/forge package. If any needed file cannot be placed under an existing root, that is an escalation, never an edit to ci/components.json.

Adding a member to application.UnitOfWork forces both store adapters to implement it in the same change, so a partial implementation does not compile. This is intended (it is what stops a store from silently lacking the aggregate) but it means the store legs cannot be deferred.

internal/domain/source_guard_test.go proves mechanically, from the AST, that no credential field and no GitHub, database or network dependency exists in internal/domain. A source locator field with a credential-shaped name, or any import reaching outward, breaks an existing test. The locator must be plain strings.

The live probe's verdict depends on an authentication state outside this repository. If gh auth has lapsed or api.github.com is unreachable at execution time, the measured result is a failure to record and escalate -- not a skip counted as a pass (G7), and not a local substitute (G3.1).

The declaration's observable_result for cap-repository-registration lists six post-registration observables (identity, Application Preview/Stable state, applied principles and repository-specific rules, Backlog state, available Runners and AI resources, whether the loop can run and why). Several have no data behind them at this commit. Each must be rendered as an explicit unobserved or not-yet-implemented state with its reason, never as a plausible-looking value; a fabricated field would be worse than an absent one.

docs/architecture/validation.md L187 records that gitleaks git scans every ref. This task creates no probe branch and pushes nothing, so it must stay that way: if any acceptance item seems to need a commit on a throwaway branch, that is the signal it belongs to stage 3 (proposed V2-072).

Editing contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml moves the contracts, api and control-plane evidence keys, and control-plane's roots are untouched. Recorded as a note under gate rule G6, resolved by V2-045; not repaired here.
